Subject: Performance commitment qualification & GPU shortlist

Hi Sanjay / Elena —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great discussion and some clear acceptance criteria came out of the call. I wanted to capture the post-call recap and propose the next steps so we can qualify your performance commitment (latency SLOs, concurrency targets, streaming expectations) and land on a dedicated capacity shortlist.

Quick summary of what we heard you need:
- Latency: 99th percentile inference <= 150ms for short-chat flows (<= 128 tokens).
- Streaming: sub-100ms first-byte for streaming-enabled assistant responses; support for chunked streaming for long responses.
- Throughput: sustained 250 qps peak (burst to 600 qps for short windows).
- Concurrency: expected 40 concurrent sessions with KV-cache reuse; effective concurrent token generation at peak ~12k tokens/sec.
- Data isolation: dedicated pool with customer tenantization and audit logs.

Proposed mutual action plan:
1) Redwood provides a short pilot bench (3-5 day perf run) using two GPU families (A100-80GB float16 / H100-80GB trimmed/quantized) + a quantized 4-bit variant. Bench will simulate your production token distribution. Attachment: dedicated-sizing-matrix.xlsx
2) We measure: p50/p95/p99 latency, streaming first-byte latency, sustained throughput curves, and token/unit cost.
3) Redwood proposes capacity recommendations and a reserve-throughput commitment to match your 99p latency SLO.
4) Sign-off on pilot results -> dedicated reservation proposal -> PO.

Can you confirm the latency and throughput numbers above reflect your expectations? Also confirm any additional legal/contractual constraints (e.g., approved cloud region, strict data residency).

Next steps: if you confirm, we will share the bench plan and schedule the perf window for the week of Apr 22.

Thanks —
Karthik

karthik@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0104

Thanks Karthik — this is super helpful. Quick clarifications from our side:
- Latency: 99p <= 150ms for short-chat is our target; for batch/rerank flows we can tolerate higher p99 (~400ms).
- Streaming: first-byte under 100ms is critical for clinician-facing assistants. We also need a flag to switch to non-streaming for certain templates.
- Throughput: 250 sustained qps is correct; we run regular spikes from nightly integrations that may reach 700 qps for 2–5 minutes.
- Concurrency: 40 active sessions is average; we can see 90–100 ephemeral workers during spikes (expect cache hit rate to matter).

One ask: can you show cost delta for A100 vs H100 vs a quantized 4-bit variant at our expected token mix? Would like a simple delta matrix in the bench results. Also please include how cached prefixes change effective throughput.

On legal: need data residency in us-east region and SOC2 evidence (we can share the vendor questionnaire after the perf window). Procurement copied.

Thanks —
Sanjay
Head of Platform Engineering — BrightBridge Health

Looping in a concise technical plan for the bench run and the GPU comparison Ben and I discussed. High-level proposal:

Bench configuration (3 days):
- Candidate 1: H100-80GB running fp16 kernels (baseline high-single-stream perf).
- Candidate 2: A100-80GB running fp16 with cuBLAS/cuDNN kernels (cost-efficient baseline).
- Candidate 3: NVLQ-quant (4-bit) on A100/H100 path using Redwood quant runtime (best cost per token).

Measurement matrix:
- Per-request: p50/p95/p99 latency for 1–128 token responses; 256/512 token trials for long-form generation.
- Streaming: first-byte latency measurement and chunk throughput; measure 95p of first-byte and average chunk delta.
- Throughput windowing: sustained qps ramps (50 -> 150 -> 250 -> 400 -> 600) with 5-minute holds and short 2-minute spikes to 700.
- Concurrency tests: 40, 80, 120 concurrent sessions with cache-hit scenarios at 20%, 50%, 80%.

Proposed reserved throughput recommendation (preliminary):
- For 99p <=150ms short-chat: H100 reserve 300 qps (sustained) or A100 reserve 450 qps if quantization tolerated.
- If strict first-byte streaming <100ms is required, H100 gives better margin for bursts.

Attachments: perf-logs-trial.tar.gz (bench logs), dedicated-sizing-matrix.xlsx (actionable numbers).

Ben — can you confirm availability for the week of Apr 22 to run the bench and own the test harness? Karthik — will schedule the trial and sign the bench statement of work once Sanjay confirms region.

—Marissa
